title: I added Dwarves and a beard customization system to my free isometric character creator on itch.io
author: TheSpriteWizard
selftext:
I've just released another update to SpriteForge, my isometric character creator and sprite-sheet generator.

**The browser version is free on** [**itch.io**](http://itch.io), so anyone interested can experiment with the character creator without downloading or purchasing anything.

https://i.redd.it/d9617a39ah0i1.png

https://i.redd.it/xqueu43fah0i1.gif

This update covers versions 0.5.2–0.5.4, and I've added quite a bit.

**What's new:**

* **Dwarves!** Male and female Dwarves are now available, bringing the collection to five customizable species: Humans, Goblins, Orcs, Elves, and Dwarves.
* **Eight new beards.** Every species can use them, not just Dwarves. They automatically fit different faces, follow the head during animations, and can be dyed independently of hairstyles.
* **Consistent sprite sizing.** I've reworked how characters are scaled and positioned. The new Locked mode keeps their feet aligned and their proportions consistent across animations and directions.
* **Better framing.** The Forge now warns when animations extend beyond the frame. I've also fixed some problems with Fit to Frame and added a Reset View button.

The sprite consistency changes were particularly important to me. When you're making a game with multiple characters, you shouldn't have to manually reposition every animation just to keep everyone standing on the same ground.

For anyone unfamiliar with the project, SpriteForge currently includes **71 animations, up to 16 rendering directions, five customizable species, and hundreds of interchangeable clothing and equipment pieces.**

**You can try the character creator free in your browser here:**

[https://thespritewizard.itch.io/sprite-forge-kanes-character-creator](https://thespritewizard.itch.io/sprite-forge-kanes-character-creator)

I'm developing this independently and continuing to expand the character library as I go.

If you give it a try, I'd appreciate some feedback, especially on how well the sprites work in your own projects.

Thanks for checking it out!

— The Sprite Wizard
